# Agent usage monitor — stories (post-feasibility)

Decisions: command `:agent-usage` / `:au`; the 2% reference is ccusage at the session level (`ccusage claude session --id <uuid>`; the `cost-state` lines are unusable as a reference: +19 to 22 %, per model, written at close only, see spike-s01.md); no task titles (meta.description, ai-title) in the MVP; keep the last line per message.id when deduplicating; read lines with a capped reader (lines up to 1.3 MB); polling tick 2 s.
Delivery order: S-01 -> S-02, S-05a -> S-03a -> S-03b, S-04 -> S-05b -> S-06 -> S-07 -> S-08.
Context: see brief.md and feasibility.md (MVP) and research.md. Effort is left blank until the
architect's feasibility pass. Rules: UI text in English US (Rule 129), numeric
aggregates only (never prompt or tool-output content).

## Epic E1 — Read agent usage from Claude Code transcripts

### S-01 — Spike: confirm the gap and the sandbox constraint
Epic : E1 — Priorité : Must — Effort : S — Plane : DEVDESK-39

En tant que mainteneur de DevDesk, je veux confirmer ce que ccusage ne fait pas et si les transcripts des sessions `sbx` sont lisibles depuis l'hôte, afin de ne pas construire un doublon.

**Critères d'acceptation**
1. Étant donné 3 sessions récentes avec sous-agents, quand ccusage est lancé dessus, alors un tableau note, pour chacune, s'il donne les tokens par sous-agent (oui/non).
2. Étant donné une session lancée dans un sandbox `sbx`, quand on cherche son transcript sur l'hôte, alors le résultat (trouvé / non trouvé, chemin) est consigné.
3. Étant donné des transcripts de deux versions de Claude Code différentes, quand on compare leurs clés `usage` et l'arborescence `subagents/`, alors les différences sont listées.
4. Le livrable tient en une page et se termine par une recommandation go / no-go.

**Hors périmètre** : tout code livré dans DevDesk.
**Questions ouvertes** : aucune.

### S-02 — Parse a session's usage per agent
Epic : E1 — Priorité : Must — Effort : M — Plane : DEVDESK-40

En tant qu'utilisateur de DevDesk, je veux que les tokens d'une session soient agrégés par agent et sous-agent, afin de savoir qui a consommé quoi.

**Critères d'acceptation**
1. Étant donné une session avec un orchestrateur et 3 sous-agents, quand elle est analysée, alors chaque agent a ses totaux in, out, cache-read et cache-write.
2. Étant donné un même `message.id` répété sur plusieurs lignes (streaming), quand il est agrégé, alors il n'est compté qu'une fois.
3. Étant donné un transcript contenant des champs inconnus, quand il est analysé, alors les champs connus sont lus et aucune erreur n'est levée.
4. Étant donné une ligne illisible ou un fichier tronqué, quand il est analysé, alors le reste est lu et l'écart est signalé.
5. Étant donné 3 sessions de référence terminées avec sous-agents, quand le total de chaque session (somme des agents : in + out + cache-read + cache-write) est comparé à `ccusage claude session --id <uuid>`, alors l'écart est inférieur à 2 % (S-01 : 0,00 % sur les 3 sessions testées). Les lignes `cost-state` ne servent pas de référence.
6. Étant donné un message de sous-agent dont la dernière ligne pour son `message.id` a `stop_reason` null, quand il est agrégé, alors son `output_tokens` est compté tel quel et l'agent est marqué « sortie partielle » : la sortie d'un sous-agent est une borne basse (S-01 : 94 % des dernières lignes sur 2.1.302, médiane de 8 tokens).
7. Étant donné une ligne dont des champs `usage` nullables (`output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`, `service_tier`, `speed`, `inference_geo`, `iterations`, `fallback_credit`) sont absents ou null, quand elle est analysée, alors ils sont lus comme optionnels et les totaux sont inchangés.
8. Étant donné une fixture synthétique « autre version » (champ `usage` renommé ou absent, type de ligne inconnu, `meta.json` sans `finished`), quand elle est analysée, alors aucune erreur n'est levée, les champs connus sont lus et l'état de l'agent est « inconnu ».
9. Étant donné une session dont le dossier contient un sous-dossier `tool-results/` à côté de `subagents/`, quand les agents sont découverts, alors `tool-results/` est ignoré et seuls les `subagents/agent-*.jsonl` sont lus.

**Hors périmètre** : coût en dollars, quota, stockage.
**Hypothèses** : validée par S-01 : `subagents/agent-*.jsonl` et `meta.json` sont restés lisibles de la même façon entre 2.1.283 et 2.1.302 (changements additifs uniquement). Le corpus ne couvre qu'une seule version mineure : la fixture « autre version » du critère 8 est donc synthétique.

## Epic E2 — The usage view

### S-03 — Browse sessions and see the agent tree
Epic : E2 — Priorité : Must — Effort : M (à livrer en deux parts) — Plane : S-03a = DEVDESK-41, S-03b = DEVDESK-42

> Redécoupage faisabilité : **S-03a** = critères 1 et 3 (liste des sessions, effort S) ; **S-03b** = critères 2 et 4 (table des agents d'une session, effort S).

En tant qu'utilisateur de DevDesk, je veux ouvrir une vue qui liste mes sessions Claude Code et affiche l'arbre des agents de la session choisie, afin de voir l'orchestration d'un coup d'œil.

**Critères d'acceptation**
1. Étant donné des sessions dans `~/.claude/projects`, quand j'ouvre la vue, alors les sessions sont listées de la plus récente à la plus ancienne avec projet et date.
2. Étant donné une session choisie, quand je la sélectionne, alors l'arbre orchestrateur → sous-agents s'affiche avec rôle, modèle et tokens par agent. Étant donné un sous-agent marqué « sortie partielle » (S-02, critère 6), alors sa valeur Out est préfixée `≥` (ex. `≥ 8`) ; celle de l'orchestrateur ne l'est pas.
3. Étant donné aucune session sur la machine, quand j'ouvre la vue, alors le tableau reste affiché avec ses en-têtes et zéro ligne (Rule 139), et le pied de page indique l'absence de session.
4. La vue respecte les règles TUI du projet : raccourcis grisés (Rule 130), aide `?` (Rule 114), redimensionnement (Rule 108).

**Hors périmètre** : tri, direct, coût.

### S-04 — Spot the most expensive agent
Epic : E2 — Priorité : Must — Effort : S — Plane : DEVDESK-43

En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux trier les agents par tokens et voir leur part du total, afin d'identifier celui qui consomme le plus.

**Critères d'acceptation**
1. Étant donné l'arbre d'une session, quand je trie par tokens, alors l'agent le plus gros est en tête. Le tri porte sur les tokens totaux (in + out + cache) : la sortie partielle des sous-agents (S-02, critère 6, ≤ 0,3 % du total) ne change pas le classement.
2. Chaque agent affiche sa part du total de la session en pourcentage, et la somme fait 100 % (± arrondi). La part est calculée sur les tokens totaux ; la valeur Out d'un sous-agent à sortie partielle reste préfixée `≥` (S-03b).
3. Étant donné deux agents du même rôle (même `agentType`), quand ils sont affichés, alors ils restent distincts.
4. Le tri utilise la touche `.` (Rule 111).

### S-05 — Follow an active session live
Epic : E2 — Priorité : Must — Effort : L (à livrer en deux parts) — Plane : S-05a = DEVDESK-44, S-05b = DEVDESK-45

> Redécoupage faisabilité : **S-05a** = lecteur incrémental sans TUI (critères 3 et 4, effort M) ; **S-05b** = polling dans la vue (critères 1, 2 et 5, effort M).

En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux que la vue se mette à jour pendant qu'une session tourne, afin de suivre la consommation sans relancer de commande.

**Critères d'acceptation**
1. Étant donné une session active, quand un agent produit un nouveau message, alors ses tokens à l'écran sont à jour en moins de 3 secondes.
2. Étant donné un nouveau sous-agent lancé, quand il apparaît, alors il s'ajoute à l'arbre sans quitter la vue.
3. Étant donné une session terminée, quand je la regarde, alors plus aucune lecture périodique n'est faite sur ses fichiers.
4. La lecture est incrémentale : un transcript de plusieurs Mo n'est pas relu en entier à chaque mise à jour.
5. `ctrl+r` force une relecture complète.

**Hypothèses** : Hypothèse: le polling (tick 2 s + stat) ne dégrade pas la réactivité de la TUI (à valider en faisabilité).

### S-06 — See each agent's activity and state
Epic : E2 — Priorité : Should — Effort : M — Plane : DEVDESK-46

En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux voir l'état, le nombre d'appels d'outils et la durée de chaque agent, afin de repérer un agent bloqué ou emballé.

**Critères d'acceptation**
1. Étant donné un agent, quand il est affiché, alors on voit son état (en cours / terminé), son nombre d'appels d'outils et sa durée.
2. Étant donné un agent sans nouvelle activité depuis plus de 5 minutes alors qu'il est « en cours », quand la vue se met à jour, alors il est signalé comme inactif.
3. Seuls des compteurs sont affichés, jamais le contenu des prompts ni des sorties d'outils.
4. Étant donné un sous-agent dont le transcript contient 5 blocs `tool_use` distincts, quand il est affiché, alors son nombre d'appels d'outils est 5, compté depuis le transcript et non depuis la notification de fin (`queued_command.usage.toolUses`, non exploitable : S-01).

### S-07 — Indicative cost per agent
Epic : E2 — Priorité : Could — Effort : M — Plane : DEVDESK-47

En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux un coût estimé par agent, afin de situer l'ordre de grandeur.

**Critères d'acceptation**
1. Étant donné un agent et son modèle, quand le coût est affiché, alors il est marqué comme estimation (tokens × tarif du modèle).
2. Étant donné un modèle au tarif inconnu, quand il est affiché, alors la cellule indique `-` et non zéro.
3. La table de tarifs est modifiable sans recompiler (configuration).
4. Le coût par agent est annoncé comme sous-estimé pour les sous-agents (leur sortie est une borne basse, S-02 critère 6, et une partie des appels API n'est pas dans les transcripts : `cache_read` 24 à 32 % plus haut dans `cost-state`). La cellule garde le marqueur d'estimation du critère 1.
5. Étant donné une session terminée dont `cost-state` est disponible, quand le coût est affiché, alors le total facturé de la session est montré avec une ligne « Unattributed » égale au total facturé moins la somme des coûts par agent (ex. total 10,00 $, agents 8,20 $ → Unattributed 1,80 $).
6. Étant donné une session en cours (pas de `cost-state`), quand le coût est affiché, alors seuls les coûts estimés par agent apparaissent, sans total facturé ni ligne « Unattributed ».

**Hors périmètre** : attribution exacte de la facture par agent, quota.

## Epic E3 — Reach sandbox sessions

### S-08 — See `sbx` sandbox sessions
Epic : E3 — Priorité : Should — Effort : S (option A) ou L (option C/B) — dépend de S-01 — Plane : DEVDESK-48

En tant qu'utilisateur travaillant en sandbox, je veux voir aussi les sessions lancées dans `sbx`, afin que la vue couvre mes longues orchestrations.

**Critères d'acceptation** : à écrire après S-01 (la solution de transport n'est pas choisie).
**Questions ouvertes** : montage de `~/.claude`, hook, ou export OpenTelemetry ?

## Won't (cette fois)
- Quota 5 h/hebdo (nécessite une statusline concurrente ; `/usage` le couvre).
- Historique persisté et comparaison par feature (pas de lien session ↔ story).
- Autres CLI d'agents, sessions cloud, OpenTelemetry.

## Backlog Plane (créé le 2026-10-24)

Projet DEVDESK, état Backlog, label `story`. Les relations « blocked by » n'ont pas pu être créées (l'API de relations répond 404 sur cette édition) : l'ordre de livraison est écrit dans chaque description.

1	# Agent usage — `internal/agentusage`
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	## What the package is for
7	
8	`internal/agentusage` reads the transcripts Claude Code writes under its
9	projects directory and returns, for one session, the **token counts per
10	agent** (the orchestrator and each sub-agent). It is the data layer of the
11	agent usage monitor (DEVDESK-40, spike S-01 then step S-02).
12	
13	What it does **not** do:
14	
15	- no cost, price or quota computation;
16	- no storage, no cache, nothing written to disk;
17	- no UI, no Bubble Tea import;
18	- no dependency beyond the Go standard library.
19	
20	**The public API is a contract.** Every exported symbol in the table below
21	(`Tokens`, `Agent`, `State`, `Usage`, `Diagnostics`, `FileIssue`, `IssueKind`,
22	`SessionFiles`, `SubAgentFiles`, `ParseSession`, `LocateSession`, `ProjectsRoot`)
23	is consumed by S-03b, S-04 and S-05a. Changing a field is a change to those
24	stories; add, do not rename.
25	
26	## Public API
27	
28	| Symbol | Role |
29	|---|---|
30	| `ProjectsRoot()` | `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects`, else `~/.claude/projects` |
31	| `LocateSession(parentTranscript)` | from `<dir>/<uuid>.jsonl`, finds `<dir>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` and their meta files. Returns `SessionFiles{ID, Parent, SubAgents}`. A missing session directory means no sub-agents. Returns an error if the parent is missing, is a symbolic link or is not a regular file. |
32	| `SessionFiles` | `ID`, `Parent` (path of the parent transcript), `SubAgents []SubAgentFiles` |
33	| `SubAgentFiles` | `ID`, `Transcript`, `Meta` (`""` if the meta file is absent) |
34	| `ParseSession(SessionFiles)` | returns `Usage`. Fails only if the parent transcript cannot be opened: a missing file, a symbolic link or a non-regular file is an **error**, not an ignored input. |
35	| `Tokens{Input, Output, CacheRead, CacheWrite}` | `int64` counters; `Total()` and `Add()` saturate at `math.MaxInt64` |
36	| `Agent` | `ID` (empty for the orchestrator), `Main`, `Type`, `Models`, `Tokens`, `Messages`, `PartialMessages`, `State`, `SpawnDepth`; `PartialOutput()` |
37	| `State` | `StateUnknown`, `StateFinished`, `StateUnfinished` |
38	| `Usage` | `SessionID`, `Agents` (orchestrator first, then sub-agents by ID), `Versions`, `Diagnostics`; `Total()` |
39	| `Diagnostics` | `UnreadableLines`, `OversizedLines`, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, `MetaMissing`, `MetaUnreadable`, `TruncatedFiles`, `Files []FileIssue`; `Degraded()` |
40	| `FileIssue{File, Offset, Kind}` | one skipped line or file problem. `File` is a base name. `Offset` is the byte offset of the line (for `IssueReadError`, the offset consumed; for `IssueOpenFailed`, 0). Entries are sorted by offset within each file. |
41	| `IssueKind` | `IssueUnreadable` (not JSON, truncated, or bad counters), `IssueOversized` (longer than `MaxLineBytes`), `IssueOpenFailed` (a sub-agent transcript could not be opened), `IssueReadError` (reading stopped on an I/O error) |
42	
43	`State` is read from the `finished` key of the sub-agent's meta file: `true`
44	is `StateFinished`, `false` is `StateUnfinished`. An absent, null or
45	wrongly typed key, a missing or unreadable meta file, and the orchestrator
46	are `StateUnknown`.
47	
48	## Transcript format
49	
50	```
51	projects/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl                          orchestrator
52	projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl     one per sub-agent
53	projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json agentType, finished, spawnDepth
54	projects/<project>/<uuid>/tool-results/                  never read
55	```
56	
57	Each transcript line is a JSON object. Only `version` and `message.{id, model,
58	stop_reason, usage}` are read; the four counters are `input_tokens`,
59	`output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.
60	Content, tools and descriptions are not declared in the decoding structs, so
61	`encoding/json` skips them without keeping them. Nothing is searched
62	recursively. Symbolic links are handled by position:
63	
64	- a **parent transcript** that is a symbolic link or not a regular file is an
65	  **error** (`LocateSession` and `ParseSession`);
66	- a sub-agent transcript that is a link or not a regular file is not listed by
67	  `LocateSession`; if one is passed to `ParseSession` anyway, it stays in
68	  `Agents` with an `IssueOpenFailed` entry;
69	- a meta file that is a link or not a regular file counts as missing
70	  (`MetaMissing`);
71	- a session directory or `subagents/` directory that is a link means no
72	  sub-agents.
73	
74	## Aggregation rules
75	
76	- **Last line wins per `message.id`**, over the whole session. Streaming writes
77	  the same message several times; only the final state counts.
78	- **A message seen in several files is attributed to the last file read**
79	  (orchestrator first, then sub-agents sorted by ID). Each such overwrite counts
80	  in `Diagnostics.CrossFileDuplicates`.
81	- **A line without `message.id` counts once**, keyed by file and offset, and
82	  increments `NoMessageID`.
83	- **`<synthetic>` is excluded**: locally generated turns are never billed.
84	- **A line with neither id, model nor usage is ignored** (user and tool-result
85	  lines).
86	- **Partial output**: a message whose last line has a null or absent
87	  `stop_reason` is counted in `Agent.PartialMessages`, and `PartialOutput()` is
88	  true. Its output count is a floor. This is computed for every agent; the UI
89	  decides how to show it.
90	- **Saturation**: sums stop at `math.MaxInt64` instead of wrapping.
91	- An incomplete last line (no newline) is not counted and its file is listed in
92	  `Diagnostics.TruncatedFiles`. If it already exceeds the line cap it is dropped
93	  silently.
94	
95	## Tolerance
96	
97	The format is not a documented API, so the parser degrades rather than fails.
98	
99	- Unknown fields are ignored.
100	- A message with an id or model but **no `usage`** (absent, or renamed by a
101	  newer client) is counted in `Diagnostics.NoUsage` and adds nothing. A
102	  sub-agent with no usable meta `finished` is `StateUnknown`.
103	- Metadata of an unexpected type (`model`, `version`, `agentType`,
104	  `spawnDepth`) costs that field only, not the line.
105	- A counter that is negative, fractional or not a number makes the line
106	  unreadable (`UnreadableLines`). An absent or null counter is 0.
107	- A sub-agent that cannot be opened stays in `Agents` with no tokens and an
108	  `IssueOpenFailed` entry. A read error mid-file keeps what was read and adds
109	  `IssueReadError` at the offset consumed.
110	- A missing meta file counts in `MetaMissing`; an unreadable one in
111	  `MetaUnreadable`.
112	
113	## Privacy
114	
115	The package returns **numeric aggregates only**. No prompt, answer, tool input,
116	description or path is ever stored in a `Usage`.
117	
118	- Errors carry the base name of a file, never its full path (`baseOnly`), and
119	  fixed messages instead of `encoding/json` errors, which can quote content.
120	- Labels that come from disk (model, version, agent type, session and agent
121	  IDs, file names) go through `sanitizeLabel`: control characters become `?`
122	  and the label is cut to 128 bytes. Text read from disk reaches a terminal,
123	  where an escape sequence would be interpreted.
124	- `FileIssue.File` is a base name, never a path.
125	- The fixtures plant `SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK` in the `content`, `description`,
126	  `cwd` and tool `input` fields of the transcripts and in the `description`
127	  of the `.meta.json` files. Tests check that it never appears in a `Usage` or
128	  an error.
129	
130	## Limits and caps
131	
132	Memory and output size do not depend on what a transcript contains.
133	
134	| Bound | Value | Behavior past it |
135	|---|---|---|
136	| Line length (`MaxLineBytes`) | 4 MiB | line skipped, counted in `OversizedLines`, never held in memory |
137	| `FileIssue` entries per file | 100, for `IssueUnreadable` and `IssueOversized` only | counters keep counting, entries stop. `IssueOpenFailed` and `IssueReadError` occur once per file and are always kept |
138	| Lines without id in the table | 100000, for the whole session (all files together) | still counted in tokens, `Messages` and `NoMessageID`, but aggregated without a table entry |
139	| Models per agent / versions per session | 64 | extra ones dropped |
140	| Label length | 128 bytes | truncated |
141	| Meta file | 1 MiB | refused (`MetaUnreadable`) |
142	
143	## Known risk: a FIFO swapped in between `Lstat` and `Open`
144	
145	`openPlain` (`safeopen.go`) calls `Lstat`, refuses links and non-regular
146	files, opens the file, then compares the handle with the `Lstat` result using
147	`os.SameFile`. That closes the check-then-open window for links. It does not
148	for a regular file replaced by a **FIFO** between `Lstat` and `Open`: `os.Open`
149	blocks until a writer appears, before `SameFile` can run. Closing it would need
150	`O_NONBLOCK`, which the `os` package does not offer portably. The window is tiny
151	and the attacker must already control the transcripts directory. Accepted and
152	documented in the code.
153	
154	## Diagnostics and `Degraded`
155	
156	`Diagnostics.Degraded()` is true if anything was skipped or guessed: unreadable
157	or oversized lines, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, meta
158	missing or unreadable, truncated files, or any `FileIssue`. A consumer should
159	show the totals as usual and flag them as approximate when it is true. A new
160	counter must be added to `Degraded()`.
161	
162	## Verification
163	
164	- **Spike S-01**: the parsing rules were checked against ccusage on 3 real
165	  sessions, with a **0.00 %** difference.
166	- **Fixtures** in `internal/agentusage/testdata/` are synthetic: shape follows
167	  Claude Code 2.1.302, every value is invented. `v2.1.302-basic/`,
168	  `synthetic-other-version/` (renamed or absent usage, unknown line type) and
169	  `damaged/` (bad line, file cut mid-JSON). Expected totals are written by hand

# Agent usage — `internal/agentusage`

> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
> read this file when working on the code it describes.

## What the package is for

`internal/agentusage` reads the transcripts Claude Code writes under its
projects directory and returns, for one session, the **token counts per
agent** (the orchestrator and each sub-agent). It is the data layer of the
agent usage monitor (DEVDESK-40, spike S-01 then step S-02).

What it does **not** do:

- no cost, price or quota computation;
- no storage, no cache, nothing written to disk;
- no UI, no Bubble Tea import;
- no dependency beyond the Go standard library.

**The public API is a contract.** Every exported symbol in the table below
(`Tokens`, `Agent`, `State`, `Usage`, `Diagnostics`, `FileIssue`, `IssueKind`,
`SessionFiles`, `SubAgentFiles`, `ParseSession`, `LocateSession`, `ProjectsRoot`)
is consumed by S-03b, S-04 and S-05a. Changing a field is a change to those
stories; add, do not rename.

## Public API

| Symbol | Role |
|---|---|
| `ProjectsRoot()` | `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects`, else `~/.claude/projects` |
| `LocateSession(parentTranscript)` | from `<dir>/<uuid>.jsonl`, finds `<dir>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` and their meta files. Returns `SessionFiles{ID, Parent, SubAgents}`. A missing session directory means no sub-agents. Returns an error if the parent is missing, is a symbolic link or is not a regular file. |
| `SessionFiles` | `ID`, `Parent` (path of the parent transcript), `SubAgents []SubAgentFiles` |
| `SubAgentFiles` | `ID`, `Transcript`, `Meta` (`""` if the meta file is absent) |
| `ParseSession(SessionFiles)` | returns `Usage`. Fails only if the parent transcript cannot be opened: a missing file, a symbolic link or a non-regular file is an **error**, not an ignored input. |
| `Tokens{Input, Output, CacheRead, CacheWrite}` | `int64` counters; `Total()` and `Add()` saturate at `math.MaxInt64` |
| `Agent` | `ID` (empty for the orchestrator), `Main`, `Type`, `Models`, `Tokens`, `Messages`, `PartialMessages`, `State`, `SpawnDepth`; `PartialOutput()` |
| `State` | `StateUnknown`, `StateFinished`, `StateUnfinished` |
| `Usage` | `SessionID`, `Agents` (orchestrator first, then sub-agents by ID), `Versions`, `Diagnostics`; `Total()` |
| `Diagnostics` | `UnreadableLines`, `OversizedLines`, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, `MetaMissing`, `MetaUnreadable`, `TruncatedFiles`, `Files []FileIssue`; `Degraded()` |
| `FileIssue{File, Offset, Kind}` | one skipped line or file problem. `File` is a base name. `Offset` is the byte offset of the line (for `IssueReadError`, the offset consumed; for `IssueOpenFailed`, 0). Entries are sorted by offset within each file. |
| `IssueKind` | `IssueUnreadable` (not JSON, truncated, or bad counters), `IssueOversized` (longer than `MaxLineBytes`), `IssueOpenFailed` (a sub-agent transcript could not be opened), `IssueReadError` (reading stopped on an I/O error) |

`State` is read from the `finished` key of the sub-agent's meta file: `true`
is `StateFinished`, `false` is `StateUnfinished`. An absent, null or
wrongly typed key, a missing or unreadable meta file, and the orchestrator
are `StateUnknown`.

## Transcript format

```
projects/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl                          orchestrator
projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl     one per sub-agent
projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json agentType, finished, spawnDepth
projects/<project>/<uuid>/tool-results/                  never read
```

Each transcript line is a JSON object. Only `version` and `message.{id, model,
stop_reason, usage}` are read; the four counters are `input_tokens`,
`output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.
Content, tools and descriptions are not declared in the decoding structs, so
`encoding/json` skips them without keeping them. Nothing is searched
recursively. Symbolic links are handled by position:

- a **parent transcript** that is a symbolic link or not a regular file is an
  **error** (`LocateSession` and `ParseSession`);
- a sub-agent transcript that is a link or not a regular file is not listed by
  `LocateSession`; if one is passed to `ParseSession` anyway, it stays in
  `Agents` with an `IssueOpenFailed` entry;
- a meta file that is a link or not a regular file counts as missing
  (`MetaMissing`);
- a session directory or `subagents/` directory that is a link means no
  sub-agents.

## Aggregation rules

- **Last line wins per `message.id`**, over the whole session. Streaming writes
  the same message several times; only the final state counts.
- **A message seen in several files is attributed to the last file read**
  (orchestrator first, then sub-agents sorted by ID). Each such overwrite counts
  in `Diagnostics.CrossFileDuplicates`.
- **A line without `message.id` counts once**, keyed by file and offset, and
  increments `NoMessageID`.
- **`<synthetic>` is excluded**: locally generated turns are never billed.
- **A line with neither id, model nor usage is ignored** (user and tool-result
  lines).
- **Partial output**: a message whose last line has a null or absent
  `stop_reason` is counted in `Agent.PartialMessages`, and `PartialOutput()` is
  true. Its output count is a floor. This is computed for every agent; the UI
  decides how to show it.
- **Saturation**: sums stop at `math.MaxInt64` instead of wrapping.
- An incomplete last line (no newline) is not counted and its file is listed in
  `Diagnostics.TruncatedFiles`. If it already exceeds the line cap it is dropped
  silently.

## Tolerance

The format is not a documented API, so the parser degrades rather than fails.

- Unknown fields are ignored.
- A message with an id or model but **no `usage`** (absent, or renamed by a
  newer client) is counted in `Diagnostics.NoUsage` and adds nothing. A
  sub-agent with no usable meta `finished` is `StateUnknown`.
- Metadata of an unexpected type (`model`, `version`, `agentType`,
  `spawnDepth`) costs that field only, not the line.
- A counter that is negative, fractional or not a number makes the line
  unreadable (`UnreadableLines`). An absent or null counter is 0.
- A sub-agent that cannot be opened stays in `Agents` with no tokens and an
  `IssueOpenFailed` entry. A read error mid-file keeps what was read and adds
  `IssueReadError` at the offset consumed.
- A missing meta file counts in `MetaMissing`; an unreadable one in
  `MetaUnreadable`.

## Privacy

The package returns **numeric aggregates only**. No prompt, answer, tool input,
description or path is ever stored in a `Usage`.

- Errors carry the base name of a file, never its full path (`baseOnly`), and
  fixed messages instead of `encoding/json` errors, which can quote content.
- Labels that come from disk (model, version, agent type, session and agent
  IDs, file names) go through `sanitizeLabel`: control characters become `?`
  and the label is cut to 128 bytes. Text read from disk reaches a terminal,
  where an escape sequence would be interpreted.
- `FileIssue.File` is a base name, never a path.
- The fixtures plant `SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK` in the `content`, `description`,
  `cwd` and tool `input` fields of the transcripts and in the `description`
  of the `.meta.json` files. Tests check that it never appears in a `Usage` or
  an error.

## Limits and caps

Memory and output size do not depend on what a transcript contains.

| Bound | Value | Behavior past it |
|---|---|---|
| Line length (`MaxLineBytes`) | 4 MiB | line skipped, counted in `OversizedLines`, never held in memory |
| `FileIssue` entries per file | 100, for `IssueUnreadable` and `IssueOversized` only | counters keep counting, entries stop. `IssueOpenFailed` and `IssueReadError` occur once per file and are always kept |
| Lines without id in the table | 100000, for the whole session (all files together) | still counted in tokens, `Messages` and `NoMessageID`, but aggregated without a table entry |
| Models per agent / versions per session | 64 | extra ones dropped |
| Label length | 128 bytes | truncated |
| Meta file | 1 MiB | refused (`MetaUnreadable`) |

## Known risk: a FIFO swapped in between `Lstat` and `Open`

`openPlain` (`safeopen.go`) calls `Lstat`, refuses links and non-regular
files, opens the file, then compares the handle with the `Lstat` result using
`os.SameFile`. That closes the check-then-open window for links. It does not
for a regular file replaced by a **FIFO** between `Lstat` and `Open`: `os.Open`
blocks until a writer appears, before `SameFile` can run. Closing it would need
`O_NONBLOCK`, which the `os` package does not offer portably. The window is tiny
and the attacker must already control the transcripts directory. Accepted and
documented in the code.

## Diagnostics and `Degraded`

`Diagnostics.Degraded()` is true if anything was skipped or guessed: unreadable
or oversized lines, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, meta
missing or unreadable, truncated files, or any `FileIssue`. A consumer should
show the totals as usual and flag them as approximate when it is true. A new
counter must be added to `Degraded()`.

## Verification

- **Spike S-01**: the parsing rules were checked against ccusage on 3 real
  sessions, with a **0.00 %** difference.
- **Fixtures** in `internal/agentusage/testdata/` are synthetic: shape follows
  Claude Code 2.1.302, every value is invented. `v2.1.302-basic/`,
  `synthetic-other-version/` (renamed or absent usage, unknown line type) and
  `damaged/` (bad line, file cut mid-JSON). Expected totals are written by hand
  in `parse_test.go`. See `testdata/README.md`.
- **Cross-check against ccusage** (step 6 of S-02, DEVDESK-54), reference
  version `ccusage@20.0.43`. `crosscheck_test.go` compares `ParseSession` with
  a reference file and is **skipped unless `DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF` is set**
  (path of the reference file). CI never sets it, so **CI does not run this
  test**: run it by hand. `DEVDESK_CLAUDE_PROJECTS` points to the projects
  directory to read (default: `ProjectsRoot()`). Each session is looked up as
  `<root>/<project>/<id>.jsonl`.
  The reference file is produced by the `mise` task:

  ```bash
  mise run agentusage-ref -- <uuid>... > /path/outside/repo/ref.json
  DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF=/path/outside/repo/ref.json go test ./internal/agentusage -run TestSessionTotalsMatchCcusage -v
  ```

  The task needs a POSIX shell, `npx` and `jq` (no Windows), and runs with
  `set -euo pipefail`: a failing ccusage call fails the task. For each session
  id it runs `ccusage claude session --id <uuid> --json` and writes
  `{"sessions": [{id, total, input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}, ...]}`,
  where `total` is ccusage's `totalTokens` and the four others are sums over its
  `entries`. Write the file **outside the repository**: it comes from real
  sessions and must never be committed.

  Only `total` is required. `input`, `output`, `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite` are
  optional per session: when present, each is compared too, and each must be
  within the tolerance (2 %, strictly below). A session whose transcript is not
  found, or whose parsing fails, fails the test.

2	
3	**Verdict : faisable, sans nouvelle dépendance Go**, à trois conditions : (1) dédupliquer par `message.id` en gardant la **dernière** ligne, (2) lire les fichiers par polling incrémental dans un `Cmd`, l'agrégat n'étant modifié que dans `Update`, (3) S-08 ne démarre qu'après une vérification sur l'hôte qui lance `sbx`.
4	Légende : [O] observé sur cette machine (structure seulement, aucun contenu lu ni rapporté), [E] estimation.

6	## Observations locales qui changent le plan
7	
8	- [O] 7 projets, 130 JSONL (178 Mo), 91 sous-agents. Plus gros fichier : 15 Mo. **Plus longue ligne : 1,27 Mo** : le `bufio.Scanner` par défaut (64 Kio) échoue. Il faut un `bufio.Reader` ou un `Scanner.Buffer` plafonné, et compter les lignes ignorées.
9	- [O] 19 types de lignes (`assistant`, `user`, `attachment`, `api-request-blob`, `cost-state`, `agent-name`…). Versions 2.1.283 à 2.1.302 seulement : les transcripts plus anciens sont purgés à 30 jours, donc la fixture « autre version » devra être **synthétique**.
10	- [O] **Dédup mesurée** sur tous les transcripts : la somme naïve gonfle les totaux ×1,9 à ×2,5. Garder la *première* ligne sous-estime `output_tokens` de 2,7 %, ce qui dépasse la tolérance de 2 %. La dernière ligne porte toujours le maximum (2968 groupes sur 2968). Il faut aussi exclure le modèle `<synthetic>`.
11	- [O] Le transcript parent ne contient aucune ligne `isSidechain` ni `agentId` : aucun double comptage entre fichiers. Le `toolUseResult` de l'outil Agent n'a pas de `usage`, mais il contient `prompt` : à ne jamais décoder.
12	- [O] `subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json` contient `finished: bool` (87 sur 91 ; absent pour un agent en cours ou une ancienne version) et `spawnDepth` (toujours 1 ici, l'arbre a donc 2 niveaux en pratique). Il contient aussi `description`, un texte de tâche, donc du contenu.
13	- [O] `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` (non documenté) : `sessionId`, `pid`, `status` (`busy` ou `idle`), `updatedAt`. C'est un bon indice pour savoir qu'une session est vivante. Repli : la date de modification du fichier.

16	- [O] Python lit les 178 Mo en 0,65 s [E : Go est du même ordre]. Une relecture complète est donc acceptable pour `ctrl+r`, mais jamais dans `Update`.

20	
21	| # | Risque | P / I | Parade |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| 1 | Format non contractuel (nouveaux types, champs renommés) | haute / haute | Décoder ligne à ligne dans une struct qui ne porte **que** des champs numériques et des identifiants, ignorer les types inconnus, compteurs `skipped` et `unknownVersion` affichés dans l'en-tête (dégradation visible). Fixtures datées et versionnées. |

Exclure `<synthetic>`. Fixer en S-01 la référence (ccusage ou `cost-state`) : si ccusage garde la première ligne, l'écart de 2,7 % est structurel. |
25	| 3 | Lecture incrémentale | moyenne / haute | Un offset par fichier ; une dernière ligne sans `\n` est gardée en reste et relue au tick suivant ; une taille inférieure à l'offset déclenche une relecture complète ; une ligne au-delà du plafond est sautée et comptée. On suppose les fichiers en ajout seul (les `compact_boundary` sont ajoutées, pas réécrites). |
26	| 4 | Polling ou watcher | moyenne / moyenne | **Polling `tea.Tick` (2 s) + `stat`**, le modèle existant (suivi du viewer, ports, conteneurs). Pas de `fsnotify` : c'est une nouvelle dépendance, peu fiable sur les montages 9p, virtiofs et WSL, précisément ceux de S-08. Ne sonder que la session ouverte et le répertoire `subagents/` (nouveaux agents). Arrêt quand la session est inactive et que tous les `finished` sont à vrai. |
27	| 5 | Règle 110 / `Update` non bloquant | faible si conçu ainsi / haute | Le `Cmd` reçoit une **copie** des offsets et rend `UsageDeltaMsg{gen, file, from, to, records}`. `Update` n'applique le delta que si `from == offset courant` et `gen` est le dernier, sinon il l'abandonne (même schéma que `toolsGen`). Une seule lecture en vol par session. `mise run test-race` est obligatoire. |
28	| 6 | Confidentialité | moyenne / haute | Les lignes contiennent prompts, thinking, `wireToolInputs`, `toolUseResult.prompt`. On ne loggue jamais une ligne, et une erreur de décodage ne cite que le fichier et l'offset. On ne compte les blocs `tool_use` que par leur `type`. `description` et `ai-title` ne s'affichent pas (voir Q3). |
29	| 7 | Intégration au routeur | faible / moyenne | Les tests de contrat attrapent les oublis (`TestEveryViewSuppliesItsHeaderAndHelp`, keymap, `AllViewNames`). Points d'entrée listés en §3. |
30	| 8 | Entrée non fiable (S-08) | moyenne / moyenne | Un sandbox écrit ces fichiers : plafond de ligne, pas de suivi des liens symboliques hors des racines, pas de décodage de chemin depuis le nom de répertoire (lire `cwd`). |

33	## 2. Effort par story
34	
35	| Story | Effort | Hypothèse qui le justifie |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| S-01 spike | **S** (½ à 1 j) | Ce document en a fait une partie (structure, dédup, `meta.json`). Reste à faire : lancer ccusage sur 3 sessions et noter sa règle de dédup, vérifier `sbx` **sur l'hôte qui le lance**, créer la fixture synthétique « autre version ». |
38	| S-02 parseur | **M** | Package pur sans TUI ; struct à champs numériques ; dédup ; tolérance ; 5 à 8 fixtures. Le critère des 2 % dépend de la référence choisie en S-01. |
39	| S-03 liste + arbre | **M**, découpage conseillé | C'est la première vue : enregistrement complet (§3). **S-03a** liste des sessions (projet = `cwd`, date = mtime, triées) : S. **S-03b** `→` vers la table des agents (orchestrateur puis sous-agents, rôle, modèle, tokens) sur le modèle runs → targets de `:jobs` : S. |

41	| S-05 direct | **L**, à redécouper | **S-05a** lecteur incrémental dans le package (offsets, reste de ligne, troncature, plafond), sans TUI : M. **S-05b** polling dans la vue (tick, `gen`, découverte des nouveaux agents, arrêt sur session terminée, `ctrl+r` = relecture complète) : M. |
42	| S-06 état / activité | **M** | État = `finished`, sinon « en cours » si la session est vivante, sinon « inconnu ». Inactif = aucune ligne depuis plus de 5 min. Compter les `tool_use` par `(message.id, apiBlockIndex)`, car les lignes streamées répètent le message. Durée = premier → dernier `timestamp`. |
43	| S-07 coût indicatif | **M** | Nouvelle section de configuration (`agent_usage.prices` par modèle, avec les tarifs distincts cache 5 min / 1 h / lecture), `-` si le tarif est inconnu. C'est une carte, pas un scalaire : la vue `:cfg` ne l'édite pas, l'édition passe par le YAML (Q4). |

46	## 3. Packages et intégration
47	
48	- `internal/agentusage` (pur, sans Bubble Tea) : `Discover(roots) []SessionRef`, `type Reader` (offsets et reste, valeur copiable), `ReadDelta(ref, offsets) (Delta, error)`, `type Aggregate` avec `Apply(Delta) Aggregate` (dédup, totaux par agent), `Liveness(ref)` (`sessions/*.json` + mtime). `internal/agentusage/pricing` arrivera avec S-07.
49	- `internal/ui/agentusage` : `Model` (deux niveaux `datatable`, fil d'Ariane sous la table, Règle 123), `availability.go` (Règle 130), `GetHelpContent` (Règle 114), les 4 méthodes de `HeaderView` (compteur de sessions et d'agents dans `GetHeaderInfo`), et l'état de chargement dans le pied de page (Règles 128 et 139).
50	- Points d'entrée : `internal/command/parser.go` (`ViewAgentUsage`, table `viewNames`), `internal/app/command_line.go` (`createView`), `docs/architecture/` (nouveau fichier, et une ligne dans le tableau de `.claude/CLAUDE.md`).
51	- **Commande** : `:usage` / `:us` (Hypothèse : `ag`, `us` et `u` sont libres, à arbitrer en Q1).

56	
57	D'après des sources tierces, les transcripts d'un `sbx` vivent dans un **volume géré par le kit** et ne sont pas sur l'hôte ; `sbx create` accepte des montages supplémentaires ([sbx/claude-mixin](https://hub.docker.com/r/sbx/claude-mixin), [DEV Community](https://dev.to/thr0n/claude-code-in-docker-sandboxes-239g)). Non vérifié : `sbx` est absent de cette machine.
58	
59	| Option | Avantages | Risques |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| **A. Monter un répertoire hôte dédié** (`~/.devdesk/agent-usage/sbx/<nom>`) comme `~/.claude/projects` du sandbox ; DevDesk le déclare comme racine supplémentaire | Aucun code de transport ; même parseur ; quasi temps réel ; survit à la suppression du sandbox | Il faut recréer le sandbox (`sbx create`) ; le sandbox écrit sur l'hôte. **Ne jamais monter tout `~/.claude`** : le sandbox pourrait écrire `settings.json`/hooks exécutés par l'hôte (évasion). Montages 9p/virtiofs : d'où le polling. |
62	| B. Lire le volume via `sbx exec … tail -c +offset` | Rien à reconfigurer côté sandbox | CLI expérimentale, un processus par tick, latence, dépend de l'auth `sbx` ; effort L |
63	| C. Hook dans le sandbox (`Stop`, `SubagentStop`) qui copie le transcript dans le dépôt monté (`.worktrees/…`) | Utilise le montage existant | Les hooks ne portent pas de tokens (il faut copier le fichier), écrit dans l'arbre du dépôt (gitignore), installe une config dans chaque sandbox, latence par événement |

1	# Agent usage — `internal/agentusage`
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	## What the package is for
7	
8	`internal/agentusage` reads the transcripts Claude Code writes under its
9	projects directory and returns, for one session, the **token counts per
10	agent** (the orchestrator and each sub-agent). It is the data layer of the
11	agent usage monitor (DEVDESK-40, spike S-01 then step S-02).
12	
13	What it does **not** do:
14	
15	- no cost, price or quota computation;
16	- no storage, no cache, nothing written to disk;
17	- no UI, no Bubble Tea import;
18	- no dependency beyond the Go standard library.
19	
20	**The public API is a contract.** Every exported symbol in the table below
21	(`Tokens`, `Agent`, `State`, `Usage`, `Diagnostics`, `FileIssue`, `IssueKind`,
22	`SessionFiles`, `SubAgentFiles`, `ParseSession`, `LocateSession`, `ProjectsRoot`)
23	is consumed by S-03b, S-04 and S-05a. Changing a field is a change to those
24	stories; add, do not rename.
25	
26	## Public API
27	
28	| Symbol | Role |
29	|---|---|
30	| `ProjectsRoot()` | `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects`, else `~/.claude/projects` |
31	| `LocateSession(parentTranscript)` | from `<dir>/<uuid>.jsonl`, finds `<dir>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` and their meta files. Returns `SessionFiles{ID, Parent, SubAgents}`. A missing session directory means no sub-agents. Returns an error if the parent is missing, is a symbolic link or is not a regular file. |
32	| `SessionFiles` | `ID`, `Parent` (path of the parent transcript), `SubAgents []SubAgentFiles` |
33	| `SubAgentFiles` | `ID`, `Transcript`, `Meta` (`""` if the meta file is absent) |
34	| `ParseSession(SessionFiles)` | returns `Usage`. Fails only if the parent transcript cannot be opened: a missing file, a symbolic link or a non-regular file is an **error**, not an ignored input. |
35	| `Tokens{Input, Output, CacheRead, CacheWrite}` | `int64` counters; `Total()` and `Add()` saturate at `math.MaxInt64` |
36	| `Agent` | `ID` (empty for the orchestrator), `Main`, `Type`, `Models`, `Tokens`, `Messages`, `PartialMessages`, `State`, `SpawnDepth`; `PartialOutput()` |
37	| `State` | `StateUnknown`, `StateFinished`, `StateUnfinished` |
38	| `Usage` | `SessionID`, `Agents` (orchestrator first, then sub-agents by ID), `Versions`, `Diagnostics`; `Total()` |
39	| `Diagnostics` | `UnreadableLines`, `OversizedLines`, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, `MetaMissing`, `MetaUnreadable`, `TruncatedFiles`, `Files []FileIssue`; `Degraded()` |
40	| `FileIssue{File, Offset, Kind}` | one skipped line or file problem. `File` is a base name. `Offset` is the byte offset of the line (for `IssueReadError`, the offset consumed; for `IssueOpenFailed`, 0). Entries are sorted by offset within each file. |
41	| `IssueKind` | `IssueUnreadable` (not JSON, truncated, or bad counters), `IssueOversized` (longer than `MaxLineBytes`), `IssueOpenFailed` (a sub-agent transcript could not be opened), `IssueReadError` (reading stopped on an I/O error) |
42	
43	`State` is read from the `finished` key of the sub-agent's meta file: `true`
44	is `StateFinished`, `false` is `StateUnfinished`. An absent, null or
45	wrongly typed key, a missing or unreadable meta file, and the orchestrator
46	are `StateUnknown`.
47	
48	## Transcript format
49	
50	```
51	projects/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl                          orchestrator
52	projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl     one per sub-agent
53	projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json agentType, finished, spawnDepth
54	projects/<project>/<uuid>/tool-results/                  never read
55	```
56	
57	Each transcript line is a JSON object. Only `version` and `message.{id, model,
58	stop_reason, usage}` are read; the four counters are `input_tokens`,
59	`output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.
60	Content, tools and descriptions are not declared in the decoding structs, so
61	`encoding/json` skips them without keeping them. Nothing is searched
62	recursively. Symbolic links are handled by position:
63	
64	- a **parent transcript** that is a symbolic link or not a regular file is an
65	  **error** (`LocateSession` and `ParseSession`);
66	- a sub-agent transcript that is a link or not a regular file is not listed by
67	  `LocateSession`; if one is passed to `ParseSession` anyway, it stays in
68	  `Agents` with an `IssueOpenFailed` entry;
69	- a meta file that is a link or not a regular file counts as missing
70	  (`MetaMissing`);
71	- a session directory or `subagents/` directory that is a link means no
72	  sub-agents.
73	
74	## Aggregation rules
75	
76	- **Last line wins per `message.id`**, over the whole session. Streaming writes
77	  the same message several times; only the final state counts.
78	- **A message seen in several files is attributed to the last file read**
79	  (orchestrator first, then sub-agents sorted by ID). Each such overwrite counts
80	  in `Diagnostics.CrossFileDuplicates`.
81	- **A line without `message.id` counts once**, keyed by file and offset, and
82	  increments `NoMessageID`.
83	- **`<synthetic>` is excluded**: locally generated turns are never billed.
84	- **A line with neither id, model nor usage is ignored** (user and tool-result
85	  lines).
86	- **Partial output**: a message whose last line has a null or absent
87	  `stop_reason` is counted in `Agent.PartialMessages`, and `PartialOutput()` is
88	  true. Its output count is a floor. This is computed for every agent; the UI
89	  decides how to show it.
90	- **Saturation**: sums stop at `math.MaxInt64` instead of wrapping.
91	- An incomplete last line (no newline) is not counted and its file is listed in
92	  `Diagnostics.TruncatedFiles`. If it already exceeds the line cap it is dropped
93	  silently.
94	
95	## Tolerance
96	
97	The format is not a documented API, so the parser degrades rather than fails.
98	
99	- Unknown fields are ignored.
100	- A message with an id or model but **no `usage`** (absent, or renamed by a
101	  newer client) is counted in `Diagnostics.NoUsage` and adds nothing. A
102	  sub-agent with no usable meta `finished` is `StateUnknown`.
103	- Metadata of an unexpected type (`model`, `version`, `agentType`,
104	  `spawnDepth`) costs that field only, not the line.
105	- A counter that is negative, fractional or not a number makes the line
106	  unreadable (`UnreadableLines`). An absent or null counter is 0.
107	- A sub-agent that cannot be opened stays in `Agents` with no tokens and an
108	  `IssueOpenFailed` entry. A read error mid-file keeps what was read and adds
109	  `IssueReadError` at the offset consumed.
110	- A missing meta file counts in `MetaMissing`; an unreadable one in
111	  `MetaUnreadable`.
112	
113	## Privacy
114	
115	The package returns **numeric aggregates only**. No prompt, answer, tool input,
116	description or path is ever stored in a `Usage`.
117	
118	- Errors carry the base name of a file, never its full path (`baseOnly`), and
119	  fixed messages instead of `encoding/json` errors, which can quote content.
120	- Labels that come from disk (model, version, agent type, session and agent
121	  IDs, file names) go through `sanitizeLabel`: control characters become `?`
122	  and the label is cut to 128 bytes. Text read from disk reaches a terminal,
123	  where an escape sequence would be interpreted.
124	- `FileIssue.File` is a base name, never a path.
125	- The fixtures plant `SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK` in the `content`, `description`,
126	  `cwd` and tool `input` fields of the transcripts and in the `description`
127	  of the `.meta.json` files. Tests check that it never appears in a `Usage` or
128	  an error.
129	
130	## Limits and caps
131	
132	Memory and output size do not depend on what a transcript contains.
133	
134	| Bound | Value | Behavior past it |
135	|---|---|---|
136	| Line length (`MaxLineBytes`) | 4 MiB | line skipped, counted in `OversizedLines`, never held in memory |
137	| `FileIssue` entries per file | 100, for `IssueUnreadable` and `IssueOversized` only | counters keep counting, entries stop. `IssueOpenFailed` and `IssueReadError` occur once per file and are always kept |
138	| Lines without id in the table | 100000, for the whole session (all files together) | still counted in tokens, `Messages` and `NoMessageID`, but aggregated without a table entry |
139	| Models per agent / versions per session | 64 | extra ones dropped |
140	| Label length | 128 bytes | truncated |
141	| Meta file | 1 MiB | refused (`MetaUnreadable`) |
142	
143	## Known risk: a FIFO swapped in between `Lstat` and `Open`
144	
145	`openPlain` (`safeopen.go`) calls `Lstat`, refuses links and non-regular
146	files, opens the file, then compares the handle with the `Lstat` result using
147	`os.SameFile`. That closes the check-then-open window for links. It does not
148	for a regular file replaced by a **FIFO** between `Lstat` and `Open`: `os.Open`
149	blocks until a writer appears, before `SameFile` can run. Closing it would need
150	`O_NONBLOCK`, which the `os` package does not offer portably. The window is tiny
151	and the attacker must already control the transcripts directory. Accepted and
152	documented in the code.
153	
154	## Diagnostics and `Degraded`
155	
156	`Diagnostics.Degraded()` is true if anything was skipped or guessed: unreadable
157	or oversized lines, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, meta
158	missing or unreadable, truncated files, or any `FileIssue`. A consumer should
159	show the totals as usual and flag them as approximate when it is true. A new
160	counter must be added to `Degraded()`.
161	
162	## Verification
163	
164	- **Spike S-01**: the parsing rules were checked against ccusage on 3 real
165	  sessions, with a **0.00 %** difference.
166	- **Fixtures** in `internal/agentusage/testdata/` are synthetic: shape follows
167	  Claude Code 2.1.302, every value is invented. `v2.1.302-basic/`,
168	  `synthetic-other-version/` (renamed or absent usage, unknown line type) and
169	  `damaged/` (bad line, file cut mid-JSON). Expected totals are written by hand
170	  in `parse_test.go`. See `testdata/README.md`.
171	- **Cross-check against ccusage** (step 6 of S-02, DEVDESK-54), reference
172	  version `ccusage@20.0.43`. `crosscheck_test.go` compares `ParseSession` with
173	  a reference file and is **skipped unless `DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF` is set**
174	  (path of the reference file). CI never sets it, so **CI does not run this
175	  test**: run it by hand. `DEVDESK_CLAUDE_PROJECTS` points to the projects
176	  directory to read (default: `ProjectsRoot()`). Each session is looked up as
177	  `<root>/<project>/<id>.jsonl`.
178	  The reference file is produced by the `mise` task:
179	
180	  ```bash
181	  mise run agentusage-ref -- <uuid>... > /path/outside/repo/ref.json
182	  DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF=/path/outside/repo/ref.json go test ./internal/agentusage -run TestSessionTotalsMatchCcusage -v
183	  ```
184	
185	  The task needs a POSIX shell, `npx` and `jq` (no Windows), and runs with
186	  `set -euo pipefail`: a failing ccusage call fails the task. For each session
187	  id it runs `ccusage claude session --id <uuid> --json` and writes
188	  `{"sessions": [{id, total, input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}, ...]}`,
189	  where `total` is ccusage's `totalTokens` and the four others are sums over its
190	  `entries`. Write the file **outside the repository**: it comes from real
191	  sessions and must never be committed.
192	
193	  Only `total` is required. `input`, `output`, `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite` are
194	  optional per session: when present, each is compared too, and each must be
195	  within the tolerance (2 %, strictly below). A session whose transcript is not
196	  found, or whose parsing fails, fails the test.
197

1	# The application shell — router, keyboard, shortcuts
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	## Bubble Tea Application Structure
7	
8	This is a **multi-view TUI application** using the Elm Architecture (TEA) pattern via Bubble Tea. Understanding the routing and view lifecycle is critical:
9	
10	**Main Components:**
11	- `main.go` - Entry point, initializes config and Bubble Tea program
12	- `internal/app/app.go` - **Router/orchestrator** that manages view switching and command mode
13	- `internal/app/messages.go` - Cross-view messages (GitLab, scan results, pull, etc.)
14	- `internal/shared/state.go` - SharedState for cross-view data (GitLab client, user, stats)
15	- `internal/ui/*/` - Individual views
16	
17	**Key Architecture Pattern:**
18	```
19	App (Router)
20	├── Manages: currentView, commandMode, viewport, sharedState
21	├── Routes messages to active view
22	├── Handles view switching via command parser
23	├── Manages multi-context configuration
24	└── Views (lazy-loaded):
25	    ├── dashboard       - Overview (stats, tools, service status)
26	    ├── status          - System monitoring (CRUD monitors)
27	    ├── git-auth        - forge authentication form (GitLab or GitHub)
28	    ├── git-explorer    - forge namespace/repository browser + multi-select clone
29	    ├── workspaces      - Local workspace management + git metadata
30	    ├── security        - Trivy + Gitleaks scanner with multi-tab results
31	    ├── containers      - Docker container list + live metrics
32	    ├── oci-resources   - OCI resource list, scan, launch containers, network inspection
33	    ├── netdiag         - Network diagnostics (Docker-based tools) + real-time port monitor
34	    ├── configuration   - Every scalar setting in the current context
35	    ├── jobs            - Long-running work: runs, then their targets
36	    ├── templates       - Catalog of repository templates: git, local or OCI sources
37	    ├── files           - Whole-filesystem browser, and the path picker forms borrow
38	    ├── about           - Which build is running, and where it keeps its files
39	    └── viewer          - One document, read-only (router-only: no `:viewer`)
40	```
41	
42	## View Switching & Command Mode
43	
44	Press `ctrl+p` to enter command mode, then type:
45	- `dashboard` or `d` - Switch to dashboard view
46	- `status` or `s` - Switch to status view
47	- `git-auth` or `ga` - Switch to the forge authentication view
48	- `git-explorer` or `ge` - Switch to the forge explorer view
49	- `workspaces` or `w` - Switch to workspaces view
50	- `security` or `sec` - Switch to security scanner view
51	- `containers`, `cont` or `ct` - Switch to containers view
52	- `oci-resources` or `oci` - Switch to OCI resources view
53	- `netdiag` or `net` - Switch to network diagnostics view
54	- `configuration`, `config` or `cfg` - Switch to the configuration view
55	- `jobs` or `j` - Switch to the jobs view: what is running, and what ran this session
56	- `templates` or `tpl` - Switch to the repository template catalog (see [templates.md](templates.md))
57	- `files` or `fs` - Browse the whole filesystem: create and delete files and directories; also the picker a form's path field opens with enter (see [filebrowser.md](filebrowser.md))
58	- `about` or `version` - Which build is running: version, commit, build date, and where the config, cache and log live
59	- `context <name>` or `ctx <name>` - Switch configuration context
60	- `context list` - Show available contexts
61	- `quit` - Exit application
62	
63	In command mode, `tab` swaps the command line for a circular breadcrumb of every view by full name (`command.ViewNames()`): ←/→ (or `tab`) move, `enter` opens, `esc` returns to the command line with its text kept. State is `App.viewPicker*`; rendering is `renderViewPicker` in `app_header.go`.
64	
65	Command parsing and tab-completion live in `internal/command/`. `ParseCommand()` returns a structured `Command{Type, View, Args}` supporting `CommandView`, `CommandContext`, `CommandQuit`, `CommandUnknown`.
66	
67	**The forge views are `git-auth` and `git-explorer`, named after the role.**
68	A context targets one forge (§3.6), so there is one authentication screen and
69	one explorer, and both adapt to whichever it is — a `gitlab-` prefix would have
70	to be typed as `github-` half the time for the same view. Their packages live
71	under `internal/ui/forge/`, which is what the import line says too.
72	
73	**The ten forge-prefixed spellings — `gitlab-auth`, `gla`, `github-auth`, `gha`
74	and their explorer counterparts, plus the older `explorer` / `exp` — no longer
75	parse at all.** They lived in a `legacyNames` table for a transition period
76	after §3.6 renamed the views, resolving without being suggested so muscle
77	memory would not break outright. That table has been removed: one spelling per
78	view, no exceptions, and `git-auth`/`ga`, `git-explorer`/`ge` are the only ones
79	a client gets.
80	
81	**There is no `:theme` command.** The theme is a setting, so the configuration
82	view owns it — the picker wrote `app.theme` behind the settings form's back,
83	which is one setting with two writers. Its overlay, `internal/app/theme.go` and
84	`CommandTheme` are all gone; `applyThemeNow` in `internal/app/configuration.go`
85	is what swaps the palette now.
86

# The application shell — router, keyboard, shortcuts

> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
> read this file when working on the code it describes.

## Bubble Tea Application Structure

This is a **multi-view TUI application** using the Elm Architecture (TEA) pattern via Bubble Tea. Understanding the routing and view lifecycle is critical:

**Main Components:**
- `main.go` - Entry point, initializes config and Bubble Tea program
- `internal/app/app.go` - **Router/orchestrator** that manages view switching and command mode
- `internal/app/messages.go` - Cross-view messages (GitLab, scan results, pull, etc.)
- `internal/shared/state.go` - SharedState for cross-view data (GitLab client, user, stats)
- `internal/ui/*/` - Individual views

**Key Architecture Pattern:**
```
App (Router)
├── Manages: currentView, commandMode, viewport, sharedState
├── Routes messages to active view
├── Handles view switching via command parser
├── Manages multi-context configuration
└── Views (lazy-loaded):
    ├── dashboard       - Overview (stats, tools, service status)
    ├── status          - System monitoring (CRUD monitors)
    ├── git-auth        - forge authentication form (GitLab or GitHub)
    ├── git-explorer    - forge namespace/repository browser + multi-select clone
    ├── workspaces      - Local workspace management + git metadata
    ├── security        - Trivy + Gitleaks scanner with multi-tab results
    ├── containers      - Docker container list + live metrics
    ├── oci-resources   - OCI resource list, scan, launch containers, network inspection
    ├── netdiag         - Network diagnostics (Docker-based tools) + real-time port monitor
    ├── configuration   - Every scalar setting in the current context
    ├── jobs            - Long-running work: runs, then their targets
    ├── templates       - Catalog of repository templates: git, local or OCI sources
    ├── files           - Whole-filesystem browser, and the path picker forms borrow
    ├── about           - Which build is running, and where it keeps its files
    └── viewer          - One document, read-only (router-only: no `:viewer`)
```

## View Switching & Command Mode

Press `ctrl+p` to enter command mode, then type:
- `dashboard` or `d` - Switch to dashboard view
- `status` or `s` - Switch to status view
- `git-auth` or `ga` - Switch to the forge authentication view
- `git-explorer` or `ge` - Switch to the forge explorer view
- `workspaces` or `w` - Switch to workspaces view
- `security` or `sec` - Switch to security scanner view
- `containers`, `cont` or `ct` - Switch to containers view
- `oci-resources` or `oci` - Switch to OCI resources view
- `netdiag` or `net` - Switch to network diagnostics view
- `configuration`, `config` or `cfg` - Switch to the configuration view
- `jobs` or `j` - Switch to the jobs view: what is running, and what ran this session
- `templates` or `tpl` - Switch to the repository template catalog (see [templates.md](templates.md))
- `files` or `fs` - Browse the whole filesystem: create and delete files and directories; also the picker a form's path field opens with enter (see [filebrowser.md](filebrowser.md))
- `about` or `version` - Which build is running: version, commit, build date, and where the config, cache and log live
- `context <name>` or `ctx <name>` - Switch configuration context
- `context list` - Show available contexts
- `quit` - Exit application

In command mode, `tab` swaps the command line for a circular breadcrumb of every view by full name (`command.ViewNames()`): ←/→ (or `tab`) move, `enter` opens, `esc` returns to the command line with its text kept. State is `App.viewPicker*`; rendering is `renderViewPicker` in `app_header.go`.

Command parsing and tab-completion live in `internal/command/`. `ParseCommand()` returns a structured `Command{Type, View, Args}` supporting `CommandView`, `CommandContext`, `CommandQuit`, `CommandUnknown`.

**The forge views are `git-auth` and `git-explorer`, named after the role.**
A context targets one forge (§3.6), so there is one authentication screen and
one explorer, and both adapt to whichever it is — a `gitlab-` prefix would have

under `internal/ui/forge/`, which is what the import line says too.

commit 8387ed03a7cf920127bc87a4d3e555f9f2db4a90
Author: anthnel <141725544+anthnel@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Sun Sep 6 13:00:11 2026 +0200

    feat: le binaire connaît sa version, publiée par release-please + goreleaser (§3.62) (#175)
    
    * feat: le binaire sait quelle version il est, et `:about` le dit (§3.62)
    
    `dk` ne savait rien de lui-même : aucune variable de version, aucun
    `-ldflags`, donc un rapport de bug ne pouvait pas nommer la build qu'il
    décrivait.
    
    `internal/version` consulte trois sources dans l'ordre — les `-ldflags`,
    les métadonnées VCS que `-buildvcs=auto` embarque, puis la version de
    module d'un `go install pkg@version` — et rien n'y écrase jamais un `-X` :
    un drapeau est une affirmation délibérée, les métadonnées un défaut. Un
    binaire qui ne sait pas répond "dev" plutôt que "v0.0.0".
    
    Seule la version passe par `-ldflags` dans mise.toml : le commit et la
    date, le compilateur les embarque déjà. `git describe` est appelé sans
    `--always`, pour qu'un dépôt sans tag réponde "dev" au lieu de promouvoir
    un SHA au rang de numéro de version.
    
    `:about` est une vue et non une touche majuscule, pour la raison que
    `:jobs` en est une (Rule 111). Elle montre le binaire et non la machine —
    les versions de Trivy et Docker restent au dashboard — donc rien n'y est
    mesuré, ce qui est aussi pourquoi `ctrl+r` n'y est pas offert (Rule 130).
    La version est au header du dashboard et d'aucun autre écran : c'est la
    vue d'accueil, la seule où elle se lit sans avoir été cherchée.
    
    L'URL du dépôt est déclarée en exception de `TestNoViewNamesAForge` : elle
    ne dépend d'aucun contexte et ne changerait pas sous GitLab.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017RSaFRQ2yT165F6GsH1GFx
    Entire-Checkpoint: fb38c45bb3ae
    
    * feat: publier une version par release-please, construire par goreleaser (§3.62)
    
    Une release se fait désormais en deux merges : release-please tient une PR
    de release à jour depuis les conventional commits, et merger cette PR crée
    le tag et la GitHub Release, à laquelle goreleaser attache les six
    binaires.
    
    release-please plutôt que semantic-release, et ce n'est pas une
    préférence : les deux lisent les mêmes commits et décident la même
    version, mais semantic-release pousse le tag directement sur `main`. Ce
    dépôt l'interdit — le mirror Entire rejette ce push, et ce refus est la
    seule protection que `main` ait puisque la branch protection est
    indisponible sur ce plan. Une release qui arrive en PR relue coûte un
    merge de plus et laisse la règle intacte.
    
    L'inconnue de la chaîne est levée : le tag naît sur GitHub, posé par
    Actions, et `git fetch origin --tags` le ramène — vérifié en posant
    v0.0.0-mirror-test par l'API. Rien n'oblige donc à taguer à la main.
    
    Le partage des rôles est écrit dans les deux configurations :
    release-please possède la version et le CHANGELOG, goreleaser les
    artefacts et rien d'autre — d'où `release.mode: append` et
    `changelog.disable: true`. `.Tag` et non `.Version` dans les ldflags,

### A progress message needs a case in the router

A message reports to the registry by implementing `jobs.Reporter`, and the
registry hears it only when `routeWork` runs — which is called from a `case`
naming the message in `App.Update`. **Implementing the interface is not enough.**
A message with no case is still delivered to its view, which is what hides the
omission: the footer says the work finished while the registry keeps the run in
progress, and `:jobs` and the footer's status line show it running for the life
of the session. The scan and then the sync of the templates view each shipped
that way.

`TestEveryJobReporterIsRoutedToTheRegistry` scans `internal/ui` for
`_ jobs.Reporter = X{}` declarations and fails naming any message the router has
no case for. Declare the compile-time proof next to the message, as the views
do, and the test finds it.

### The broadcast, and the one spinner chain

Views never hold a pointer to the registry. The router hands them a snapshot in
`jobs.ChangedMsg`, so nothing is read from `View()` while something else writes
it, and a view holding a snapshot cannot write back — every mutation goes
through the one owner.

`broadcastJobs` updates **every held view**, on screen or not, so coming back to
one shows what happened while it was away without it having to ask; the layout
is re-measured once at the end, since only the view on screen can change the
footer's height. `sendJobsTo` covers the remaining case: a view built lazily on
the way in was there for none of it, so `switchView` hands it the snapshot.

There is **one** spinner chain for the whole application, the router's
(`jobTickMsg`, `ensureJobTick`, `handleJobTick`). It is alive exactly while
`Running() > 0` and stops by not being renewed; a chain is identified by a
sequence number, so a tick from one already replaced is dropped and a second
chain is impossible rather than merely unlikely. The frame travels in the
message **bare** — Rule 122, because a view puts it in a table cell, which is
measured before it is styled — and `RenderedFrame()` is the styled reading a
footer takes (Rule 128).

This is what removes the four hand-stamped frames, and with them the failure
each of them could produce: a chain that died on the first idle tick with
nothing able to restart it, leaving the spinner frozen on the frame it died at.


### The `:jobs` view — `internal/ui/jobsview`

The reader's side of the registry, and it owns nothing: it starts no work, holds
no timer and fetches nothing. Its rows are the snapshot, so there is nothing to
refresh — `ctrl+r` is absent rather than greyed, because there is no operation
behind it to be unavailable.

41	// InterfacesModel is the tab that lists this machine's network interfaces.
42	//
43	// It was the Topology tab, which showed four sections read from ip and
44	// iptables in containers started with --network host — that is, the Docker
45	// Desktop VM's network and not the machine's (D57). Three of the four sections
46	// were removed rather than translated, because nothing portable produces them
47	// (§3.44); the route question moved to the Diagnostics pipeline, where it is
48	// asked about a target rather than in the abstract. What is left is what reads
49	// natively everywhere, so the tab is named after it.
50	type InterfacesModel struct {
51		width  int
52		height int
53	
54		table   datatable.Model[netiface.Interface]
55		spinner spinner.Model
56	
57		loading bool
58		// lastOK dates the rows, and loadErr says the most recent read failed.
59		//
60		// A failed read keeps the rows on screen: they are not wrong, they are
61		// dated, and dropping them would leave the tab empty over a transient
62		// failure. What has to be said is their age — a footer *message* cannot
63		// carry it, since it expires after three seconds (Rule 128).
64		lastOK  time.Time
65		loadErr bool
66	
67		// footer is this tab's own message line. Each tab keeps one: a shared
68		// instance would let a message set here outlive the switch away from it.
69		footer components.FooterMessage
70	}
71	
72	func newInterfacesModel() *InterfacesModel {
73		sp := spinner.New()
74		sp.Spinner = spinner.Dot
75		sp.Style = theme.SpinnerStyle()
76	
77		return &InterfacesModel{
78			loading: true,
79			spinner: sp,
80			table: datatable.New(datatable.Config[netiface.Interface]{
81				Columns:    interfaceColumns(),
82				SortColumn: 0,
83			}),
84		}
85	}
86	
87	// interfaceColumns describes the interfaces table.
88	//
89	// The MAC is here because net.Interfaces() hands it over for nothing and the
90	// old tab threw it away — it is what a DHCP lease, a switch port and an asset
91	// inventory are all keyed on, so it is the field someone comes to this screen
92	// to copy.
93	func interfaceColumns() []datatable.Column[netiface.Interface] {
94		name := datatable.Column[netiface.Interface]{
95			Title: "Interface", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 16,
96			Cell:   func(i netiface.Interface) string { return i.Name },
97			Search: func(i netiface.Interface) string { return i.Name },
98			Less:   func(a, b netiface.Interface) bool { return a.Name < b.Name },
99		}

what Claude Code 2.1.302 writes under `~/.claude/projects/`, but every value is
invented. No real prompt, answer, path, description or token count was copied.
`SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK` sits in the `content`, `description`, `cwd` and tool
`input` fields of the transcripts, and in the `description` of the `.meta.json`
files, on purpose: a test checks that it never reaches a `Usage` value or an
error.

Layout: `<fixture>/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl`, sub-agents in
`<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` with `agent-<id>.meta.json` beside them.

| Fixture | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `v2.1.302-basic/` | orchestrator + 3 sub-agents, streaming repeats, null/absent usage fields, a `<synthetic>` message, a partial last message, and a `tool-results/` folder that must not be read |
| `synthetic-other-version/` | an invented "9.0.0": renamed or absent `usage`, unknown line type, `meta.json` without `finished` |
| `damaged/` | a non-JSON line in the middle of a file and a sub-agent file cut mid-JSON without a final newline |

Expected totals are written by hand in `parse_test.go`, not computed from these files.

680	// routeToView hands a message to a named view whether or not it is on screen,
681	// without changing which view is. Work started in a view has to finish there:
682	// its progress markers, its spinner and its cache write all live in its model,
683	// so a message dropped because the user walked away leaves a row marked busy
684	// for the life of the view.
685	//
686	// It does not re-measure the layout the way forwardToActiveView does — a view
687	// the user is not looking at cannot change the footer's shape on screen, and
688	// it is measured on its way back in (switchView asks for a resize).
689	func (a *App) routeToView(target command.ViewType, msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
690		view, ok := a.views[target]
691		if !ok {
692			return a, nil
693		}
694		updatedView, cmd := view.Update(msg)
695		a.views[target] = updatedView
696		return a, cmd
697	}

# Agent usage S-02: parse a session's usage per agent (DEVDESK-40)

Package `internal/agentusage`, stdlib only, no UI dependency. Plane tasks DEVDESK-49..54.

## Steps

1. (49) Capped line reader (`scanLines`, 4 MiB max) and `Tokens`.
2. (50) `decodeLine` (record decoding) plus a fuzz test.
3. (51) `meta.json` reading, `LocateSession` / `ProjectsRoot`.
4. (52) Aggregation, last line wins.
5. (53) `ParseSession` with fixtures (basic, other-version, damaged) and a sentinel test.
6. (54) ccusage cross-check test (`DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF`, skipped by default), `agentusage-ref` mise task, `docs/architecture/agent-usage.md`, a line in `.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

## Public interfaces (contract for S-03b / S-04 / S-05a)

- `Tokens{Input, Output, CacheRead, CacheWrite int64}` with `Total()` and `Add()`.
- `Agent{ID, Main, Type, Models, Tokens, Messages, PartialMessages, State, SpawnDepth}`, with `PartialOutput()` (true when `PartialMessages > 0`).
- `Usage{SessionID, Agents, Versions, Diagnostics}`. `Versions` is the list of distinct transcript versions seen (at most 64); there is no counter of "unknown versions".
- `Diagnostics{UnreadableLines, OversizedLines, NoUsage, NoMessageID, CrossFileDuplicates, MetaMissing, MetaUnreadable, TruncatedFiles []string, Files []FileIssue}` and `Degraded()`.
- `FileIssue{File (base name), Offset, Kind}` with `IssueKind` = `IssueUnreadable`, `IssueOversized`, `IssueOpenFailed`, `IssueReadError`.

These field lists are final; keep them stable.

## Assumptions

- Max line length is 4 MiB (`MaxLineBytes`); longer complete lines are skipped and counted as oversized.
- A record without `message.id` is counted once (`NoMessageID`).
- `NoUsage` counts a record with a non-empty `message.id` OR a non-empty `model` but no `usage`.
- A missing `stop_reason` means the output is partial.
- Symlinks and non-regular files are refused (no FIFO is opened). A FIFO swapped in between the check and the open (TOCTOU) is accepted as a known residual risk.

# Agent usage S-03a: list Claude Code sessions in `:agent-usage` / `:au` (DEVDESK-41)

Story: a view that lists the Claude Code sessions under the projects root, newest
first, with project (= `cwd`) and date (= mtime). Empty root: the table stays
(headers, zero rows, Rule 139) and the footer says there is no session. Rules
130, 114, 108. Out of scope: sort, live, cost, agent tree (S-03b = DEVDESK-42).

## What exists today (checked on `main` @ 7d6b9a2)

- **No view, no command.** No `ViewAgentUsage`, no `agent-usage`/`au` in
  `internal/command/parser.go`, no `internal/ui/agentusage*` package. `au` is a
  free alias. This story **creates** the view and registers it; it is the
  first view of the feature.
- `internal/agentusage` (DEVDESK-40) has `ProjectsRoot`, `LocateSession`,
  `ParseSession`. **It cannot list sessions:** the `Discover(roots)` that
  feasibility.md §3 names was never built, and the incremental reader (S-05a,
  DEVDESK-44) does not exist yet. Step 1 adds the listing.
- **`cwd` is a sentinel field today.** The fixtures put `SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK`
  in `cwd`, and agent-usage.md says "no ... path is ever stored in a Usage".
  Showing the project means reading `cwd`. That needs a new type, not a
  `Usage`, and an amended privacy note (see Q1).
- Reference views: `internal/ui/netdiag/interfaces_model.go` (async load,
  own spinner, footer `Status`, `ctrl+r`, body = `table.View()`) and
  `internal/ui/jobsview` (package layout, help, tests, `FilterBarVisible`).

## Questions bloquantes

**Q1. How much of `cwd` is shown in the Project column?** This changes the
package's privacy contract, which today treats `cwd` as content that must never
leak.
- **A (recommended)**: the full path with home folded (`~/projects/x/devdesk`),
  truncated from the left when the column is narrow. It tells apart two projects
  with the same last segment, and the user sees only their own machine.
- B: the last segment only (`devdesk`). Shows less in screenshots, but two
  `api/` directories look the same.
- C: the encoded directory name (`-home-…-devdesk`), without reading the
  transcript. Lossy (`/` and `.` both become `-`), and it still holds the full
  path.

The plan assumes A. Picking B only changes the Project `Cell` and one test.

## Assumptions (no impact outside this story; reversible)

- H1. View package `internal/ui/agentusageview` (package `agentusageview`). It
  follows the `internal/jobs` / `internal/ui/jobsview` pattern and avoids an
  import alias against `internal/agentusage`.
- H2. Date = mtime of the **parent** transcript (`<uuid>.jsonl`), sub-agents not
  looked at. Column "Last active", absolute local time `2006-01-02 15:04` (as in
  `status/columns.go`).
- H3. Project = the first non-empty string `cwd` in the parent transcript. Read
  at most `cwdProbeBytes` = 8 MiB (2 × `MaxLineBytes`), so one 4 MiB line can be
  skipped. If none is found: `-` in DimStyle. The directory name is never
  decoded (feasibility risk 8).
- H4. Extra `Session` column: the first 8 characters of the id, `Optional`.
  Without it, two sessions of the same project look the same. `/` matches the
  full id.
- H5. No `.` sort in S-03a (out of scope). The order comes from the package
  (mtime descending, then ID ascending). No column has a `Less`. The table uses
  `SortColumn: -1`.
- H6. `ctrl+r` lists again. **Opening the view lists again too** (`Init` runs on
  every `switchView`). This is also the fix for a result that arrives while
  another view is on screen: the router hands it to that other view
  (`forwardToActiveView`), which drops it, and the next visit lists again. No
  router case.
- H7. A file named `agent-*.jsonl` directly under a project directory is not a
  session (older layout). It is skipped and not counted.
- H8. The root itself may be a symlink (dotfiles), so it is followed with
  `os.Stat`. Below the root, a symlinked project directory or transcript is
  refused and counted in `Omitted`, as in `LocateSession`.
- H9. At most `maxSessions` = 10000 sessions are kept. All entries are `stat`ed
  and sorted, the newest are kept, and only those are read for `cwd`. The rest
  count in `Omitted`.
- H10. Rule 130 in S-03a: no key here depends on the row. The column is
  `ctrl+r Refresh`, `/ Filter`, `? Help`, never greyed (an operation in
  progress is not a reason to grey, per Rule 130), and the same in every state.
  `availability.go` arrives with S-03b's `→`. Announcing `→` now would bind it
